cards.title: React Inline Styles
cards.content:
In React, inline styles are not passed as standard CSS strings. Instead, they are defined using a JavaScript object where key names are camelCased versions of CSS properties.

const divStyle = {
  color: "blue",
  backgroundColor: "lightgray",
  fontSize: "16px"
};

function MyComponent() {
  return <div style={divStyle}>Styled Text</div>;
}

Note that values are generally strings, but pixel values can often be passed as numbers (e.g., fontSize: 16).

cards.title: CSS Modules
cards.content:
CSS Modules allow you to write traditional CSS files but scope them locally to the component. This prevents class name collisions across your application.

When imported, the CSS classes become properties of a JavaScript object, which you reference in your JSX.

/* Button.module.css */
.errorButton {
  background-color: red;
}
/* Button.jsx */
import styles from './Button.module.css';

export function Button() {
  return <button className={styles.errorButton}>Delete</button>;
}

cards.title: CSS-in-JS & Styled Components
cards.content:
Styled Components is a popular CSS-in-JS library that uses tagged template literals to style components directly in your JavaScript files.

import styled from 'styled-components';

const StyledButton = styled.button`
  background: ${props => props.$primary ? "blue" : "white"};
  color: ${props => props.$primary ? "white" : "blue"};
  padding: 8px 16px;
  border: 2px solid blue;
`;

// Usage:
// <StyledButton $primary>Click Me</StyledButton>

It automatically handles vendor prefixing, unique class names, and easily allows dynamic styling based on component props.

pairs.right: Passed as an object with camelCase properties, fast but cannot handle pseudo-selectors.
Traditional CSS syntax hashed at build-time to guarantee local scoping.
CSS-in-JS approach offering prop-driven dynamic styling in JS files.
Utility-first framework styling components using pre-configured atomic classes.

cards.title: Tailwind CSS in React
cards.content:
Tailwind CSS is a utility-first CSS framework. Instead of writing custom CSS, you apply pre-defined utility classes directly to elements inside your className prop.

export default function Card() {
  return (
    <div className="max-w-sm rounded overflow-hidden shadow-lg p-6 bg-white">
      <h2 className="font-bold text-xl mb-2">React + Tailwind</h2>
      <p className="text-gray-700 text-base">Easy styling without leaving JSX!</p>
    </div>
  );
}

This approach minimizes the size of your final production CSS build since unused utilities are automatically purged.
